source.prompt: Instrumental background music for a classic 1990s-style Japanese fantasy role-playing game. The writing and orchestration evoke the golden age of 16-bit console RPG soundtracks (memorable singable lead melody, clear bass line, warm chords, tasteful hall reverb), but the production is high quality, warm and full, recorded with real-sounding instruments. Completely original melody. The game's world lives in an endless night lit by lanterns, lamps and great beacon fires; the score is gentle and melancholic, with warmth and a quiet, stubborn hope. A high plateau under a sky full of stars and its academy town of star-readers: an observatory dome, brass telescopes and star charts, wind over the highland grass, an old sage who counted every star. Wondering, celestial and scholarly, a gentle 3/4 waltz with a sense of quiet curiosity and wide open sky. Tempo 84 BPM, 3/4 time, key of B-flat major (lydian colour). Instrumentation: celesta and harp, glass-harmonica-like pad, solo clarinet melody, pizzicato and soft bowed strings, music box, light triangle, a soft french horn. Form: celesta and harp pickup; section A clarinet waltz melody; section B strings and horn, a little wistful; a music-box interlude; section A again with fuller strings. Duration: 90 seconds. Instrumental only: no vocals, no singing, no spoken words, no lyrics. Keep one steady tempo and key from start to finish, no fade-in and no fade-out, no long silences; the last bar leads naturally back into the first bar so the piece loops seamlessly as game background music.
